title: Gravitational lens
description: Drag a point-mass lens across a galaxy atlas. Watch a spiral stretch into arcs and split into multiple images.
hint: Drag to move the lens; arrow keys make fine adjustments. Switch Lens off to compare the exact same sky. Enable the source grid to see the geometry bend.
explanation: Each pixel traces an observed image angle back to the source atlas with the point-mass thin-lens equation: β = θ − θE²(θ − lens)/|θ − lens|². The blue spiral becomes arcs near alignment; off-axis galaxies produce a larger image and an inverted secondary image. Relative mass scales θE² at fixed distances. This dimensionless, weak-field, geometric-optics approximation uses a procedural source atlas and a tiny numerical floor at the point singularity. The crosshair marks the lens, and the constellation and grid are visual guides. It does not model strong-field black-hole optics or an accretion disk. Both views keep identical exposure and a fixed source atlas.

title: Volumetric nebula
description: Fly through layered clouds of interstellar color, integrated along a camera ray.
hint: Move the pointer to change the viewing direction. Density changes how light accumulates.
explanation: Each invocation marches through a three-dimensional fractal-noise density field. Front-to-back emission and absorption accumulate into a translucent nebula. The density slider changes optical depth rather than simply adjusting brightness.

title: Aurora curtains
description: Folded ribbons of atmospheric light drape above a quiet horizon.
hint: Move to steer the curtain. Change the fold frequency and pause the light.
explanation: A camera ray integrates many thin emissive layers. A warped ridge field defines the auroral curtain, while altitude controls its green-to-magenta emission. This is an artistic atmospheric model.

title: Ocean caustics
description: Refracted light gathers into an intricate lattice under a moving water surface.
hint: Move to change the light direction. Sharpness controls the concentrated ridges.
explanation: Several directional waves form a surface slope field. Its local derivative compresses light into bright caustic ridges. The result is a real-time approximation of underwater light concentration, not a full optical ray trace.

title: Mandelbulb explorer
description: A rotating, self-similar three-dimensional world carved by a distance estimator.
hint: Move horizontally to orbit the fractal. Power changes the geometry itself.
explanation: A spherical-coordinate power map iterates a three-dimensional escape-time fractal. Its distance estimate drives sphere tracing; nearby samples estimate a surface normal for lighting. Iteration and step counts are bounded for interactive rendering.

title: Newton basins
description: Three roots divide the complex plane into infinitely folded regions of attraction.
hint: Move to pan the complex plane. Zoom into the borders between the three roots.
explanation: Each pixel applies Newton’s method to z³ − 1. The converged root selects its color; the number of iterations controls the banding. The intricate boundaries arise from convergence, not from a painted texture.

title: Voronoi stained glass
description: Moving sites tessellate the plane into luminous, irregular panes.
hint: Move the pointer to change the light spot. Density changes the number of cells.
explanation: A 3 × 3 search finds the nearest and second-nearest animated feature points. Their distance gap draws the leaded seams, while a hash assigns each pane a stable jewel color.

title: Diffraction aperture
description: Coherent waves from a slit array interfere into colored diffraction bands.
hint: Move to alter slit spacing. The control changes how many coherent apertures contribute.
explanation: The kernel sums complex amplitudes from a finite, equally spaced slit array for three wavelengths, then squares their magnitudes to obtain intensity. A single-slit sinc envelope modulates the result. It is a dimensionless far-field model, not a calibrated optical instrument.

title: Curl-flow streamlines
description: Fine threads trace a divergence-free flow field like ink stretched through water.
hint: Move the pointer to bend the flow. Complexity changes the vector field, not chemical reactions.
explanation: Finite differences of a scalar potential define a two-dimensional curl field. Every pixel integrates a short path through it and accumulates thin dye-like marks. This is streamline integration, distinct from the reaction-diffusion example.

title: Contour terrain
description: A miniature world rises from a height field, etched with survey-like elevation lines.
hint: Move horizontally to orbit. Relief changes the landscape’s actual elevation.
explanation: A camera ray intersects a multi-octave height field. Finite differences estimate normals, while quantized elevation draws contour lines. The relief slider changes both the silhouette and the shadowed surface.
